t: A Welsh kingdom formed in the old territory of the Cornovii after Roman rule ended, centred on the upper Severn and the hills of mid Wales.
For three centuries it bore the brunt of Mercian expansion, losing its eastern lowlands; Offa’s Dyke was built along its frontier.
Its dynasty revived under Bleddyn ap Cynfyn and Madog ap Maredudd, but the kingdom was divided into two after Madog died in 1160.
dyk: The inscription on the Pillar of Eliseg is now almost illegible; its text is known mainly because the scholar Edward Lhuyd copied it in 1696.
ev: King Selyf ap Cynan is killed at the Battle of Chester against Æthelfrith of Northumbria
Offa of Mercia builds Offa’s Dyke along the frontier with Powys
The Mercians take Powys ‘into their power’, according to the Annales Cambriae
Cyngen ap Cadell, last of the old line, dies on pilgrimage at Rome
Bleddyn ap Cynfyn becomes ruler of Powys and Gwynedd
Madog ap Maredudd leads Welsh troops for Ranulf of Chester at the Battle of Lincoln
Madog dies and Powys is divided into Powys Fadog and Powys Wenwynwyn
